newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen says E-Plus stake not for sale.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen says E-Plus stake not for sale.

text.p: German steel and engineering group Thyssen AG on Monday sought to dismiss speculation it could put its mobile communications unit on the block, saying its stake in E-Plus Mobilfunk GmbH was not for sale.

The comments came after the weekly news magazine Focus said utility RWE AG has offered to buy Thyssen's 30 percent stake in E-Plus for some 3.5 billion marks ($2.27 billion). Thyssen is set to outline its new telecoms strategy on Tuesday.
Sources close to RWE said the company has made an offer to buy the E-Plus stake, but that the bid was between 2.5 billion and three billion marks.
While confirming that talks with RWE and its telecoms partner Veba were still underway, Thyssen denied that RWE has made any offer.
"There is no offer from RWE," Thyssen spokesman Reiner Hochscheid told Reuters. "We do not intend to sell E-Plus."
In addition to Thyssen, E-Plus shareholders include Veba AG, BellSouth and Vodafone.

Thyssen has come under pressure to clarify its strategy for entering the telecommunications market after losing to Mannesmann earlier this year in a bid for a 49.8 percent stake in the telecoms subsidiary of the German railway.
Thyssen has stated that it still plans to make major investments in telecommunications and to list some shares in its subsidiary Thyssen Telecom AG.
Thyssen Telecom will hold a news conference on Tuesday to outline its telecommunications strategy. The company is not expected to make any major announcements.
